title: Rabbi Zevida
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni, end of chapter 1: Rabbi Zevida was sitting and teaching his son; Rabbi Krospa passed by and said to him, “Do not teach it to him so,” etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 7:4: “Rabbi Yochanan said … Rabbi Zevida said: And properly so.” In Jerusalem Talmud Orlah 1:5: Rabbi Zevida ruled concerning these unripe dates that they should be buried; Rabbi Yonah asked: “If he went ahead and redeemed them, are they not redeemed? Yet you say they require burial?” Hyman infers that he was senior to Rabbi Yonah. In Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 8:7: “Rabbi Zevida said: Rabbi Yasa raises a difficulty”; in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 9:7 he spoke in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Mamal; in Shemot Rabbah 44:9: “Rabbi Zevida said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said.” He is likewise mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 10:4, saying that a baraita supports Rabbi Yochanan.

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud. גדול מן is rendered senior here; the inference about Yonah’s generation is Hyman’s, not a claim of intellectual superiority. The burial/redemption question remains a question.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Orlah 1:5 directly names Zevida and has Yonah ask about redemption and burial. Its עבר ופדיו is a went-ahead-and-redeemed construction; the question is rhetorical, not a newly asserted failure of redemption. Hyman’s inference of seniority remains his, not independent chronology.
